answer.rationale: Primary objective is sustained availability without losing customer writes. Rollback is ruled out by compliance. Regional failover (memory_b2) is effective for broad degradation but today's issue is concentrated on the write path while settlements are at daily peak — shifting traffic mid-peak risks amplifying write loss. Adding capacity doesn't address an already-deployed bad-build symptom and won't beat the latency curve in time. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) helps dashboards, not write p99. Circuit breakers on the write-path dependencies (memory_b4) contain the blast radius, fail fast, and preserve the rest of the checkout path — which is the same containment pattern that saved us during the partner outage. Rolling out narrowly and guarded buys time to diagnose whether the new build introduced a dependency-level regression, while keeping customer writes flowing on the healthy code path. Memory_b2 is worth verifying as a fallback only; not the first move. Memory_b1 (rollback) is informational but irrelevant — compliance blocks that path. Verification of memory_b4 confirms the containment pattern transfers cleanly to write-path dependencies; memory_b2 is pulled so a fast failover remains an option if the breaker doesn't bend the curve.
